sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Triangle with sides $5$, $7$ and included angle $60^\circ$. Find the third side (Law of Cosines).
questions.answer: Final Answer: $\sqrt{39}$. $c^2=5^2+7^2-2(5)(7)\cos60^\circ=39\Rightarrow c=\sqrt{39}$.

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$ studying properties of equality and congruence, $m\angle A = 39^\circ$ and $m\angle B = 45^\circ$. What is $m\angle C$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $96^\circ$. Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (39^\circ + 45^\circ) = 96^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (39^\circ + 45^\circ) = 96^\circ$.

questions.q: A triangle has two sides $7$ and $12$. Which inequality must the third side $x$ satisfy? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: 5<x<19. By the triangle inequality, $|12-7|<x<7+12\Rightarrow 5<x<19$.
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, $|12-7|<x<7+12\Rightarrow 5<x<19$.

questions.q: Classify the triangle with sides $7$, $8$, $9$.
questions.answer: Final Answer: Acute triangle. Largest side squared $9^2=81$ vs sum of squares $7^2+8^2=113\Rightarrow$ acute.
questions.explanation: Largest side squared $9^2=81$ vs sum of squares $7^2+8^2=113\Rightarrow$ acute.

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$ studying proving angle relationships, $m\angle A = 41^\circ$ and $m\angle B = 45^\circ$. What is $m\angle C$? Show your complete algebraic work.
questions.answer: Final Answer: $94^\circ$. Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (41^\circ + 45^\circ) = 94^\circ$.
questions.explanation: Using the triangle angle-sum theorem, $m\angle C = 180^\circ - (41^\circ + 45^\circ) = 94^\circ$.

questions.q: Two parallel lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ are cut by a transversal $T$. A pair of alternate exterior angles are given by $(7x - 14)^{\circ}$ and $(4x + 31)^{\circ}$. Find the value of $x$ and the measure of each alternate exterior angle.
questions.answer: Step 1: Set up the equation using alternate exterior angles: Alternate exterior angles created by parallel lines are congruent: $7x - 14 = 4x + 31 \Rightarrow 3x = 45 \Rightarrow x = 15.$ Step 2: Evaluate the angle measure: $7(15) - 14 = 105 - 14 = 91^{\circ}.$ Check: $4(15) + 31 = 60 + 31 = 91^{\circ}$. Both alternate exterior angles measure $91^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Set up the equation using alternate exterior angles: Alternate exterior angles created by parallel lines are congruent: $7x - 14 = 4x + 31 \Rightarrow 3x = 45 \Rightarrow x = 15.$ Step 2: Evaluate the angle measure: $7(15) - 14 = 105 - 14 = 91^{\circ}.$ Check: $4(15) + 31 = 60 + 31 = 91^{\circ}$. Both alternate exterior angles measure $91^{\circ}$.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal line. Two consecutive interior angles have measures $(3x - 10)^{\circ}$ and $(2x + 25)^{\circ}$. Find the measure of the acute angle.
questions.answer: Solution: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$: $(3x - 10) + (2x + 25) = 180 \Rightarrow 5x + 15 = 180 \Rightarrow 5x = 165 \Rightarrow x = 33.$ Substitute $x = 33$ into both angle expressions: $3(33) - 10 = 89^{\circ}, \quad 2(33) + 25 = 91^{\circ}.$ The acute angle has measure $89^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Solution: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$: $(3x - 10) + (2x + 25) = 180 \Rightarrow 5x + 15 = 180 \Rightarrow 5x = 165 \Rightarrow x = 33.$ Substitute $x = 33$ into both angle expressions: $3(33) - 10 = 89^{\circ}, \quad 2(33) + 25 = 91^{\circ}.$ The acute angle has measure $89^{\circ}$.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: Triangle with sides $6$, $8$ and included angle $30^\circ$. Find its area.
questions.answer: Final Answer: 12. $A=\frac{1}{2}(6)(8)\sin30^\circ=12$.

questions.q: Two angles $\angle P$ and $\angle Q$ form a linear pair. If $m\angle P = (4x + 12)^{\circ}$ and $m\angle Q = (2x + 18)^{\circ}$, find the measure of the smaller angle.
questions.answer: Solution: Since they form a linear pair, their measures sum to $180^{\circ}$: $(4x + 12) + (2x + 18) = 180 \Rightarrow 6x + 30 = 180 \Rightarrow 6x = 150 \Rightarrow x = 25.$ Now substitute $x = 25$ back into each expression: $m\angle P = 4(25) + 12 = 112^{\circ}, \quad m\angle Q = 2(25) + 18 = 68^{\circ}.$ The smaller angle has measure $68^{\circ}$.
questions.explanation: Solution: Since they form a linear pair, their measures sum to $180^{\circ}$: $(4x + 12) + (2x + 18) = 180 \Rightarrow 6x + 30 = 180 \Rightarrow 6x = 150 \Rightarrow x = 25.$ Now substitute $x = 25$ back into each expression: $m\angle P = 4(25) + 12 = 112^{\circ}, \quad m\angle Q = 2(25) + 18 = 68^{\circ}.$ The smaller angle has measure $68^{\circ}$.

questions.q: Two angles $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ are vertical angles. If $m\angle 1 = (5x - 23)^{\circ}$ and $m\angle 2 = (3x + 17)^{\circ}$, find the measure of $m\angle 1$ and the measure of its supplement.
questions.answer: Step 1: Set up the equation using vertical angles: Since vertical angles are equal in measure: $5x - 23 = 3x + 17 \Rightarrow 2x = 40 \Rightarrow x = 20.$ Step 2: Find the measure of $m\angle 1$: $m\angle 1 = 5(20) - 23 = 100 - 23 = 77^{\circ}.$ Step 3: Find its supplement: $180^{\circ} - 77^{\circ} = 103^{\circ}.$
questions.explanation: Step 1: Set up the equation using vertical angles: Since vertical angles are equal in measure: $5x - 23 = 3x + 17 \Rightarrow 2x = 40 \Rightarrow x = 20.$ Step 2: Find the measure of $m\angle 1$: $m\angle 1 = 5(20) - 23 = 100 - 23 = 77^{\circ}.$ Step 3: Find its supplement: $180^{\circ} - 77^{\circ} = 103^{\circ}.$

questions.q: In $\Delta  ABC$, the exterior angle at vertex $C$ measures $134^{\circ}$. The two remote interior angles have measures $m\angle A = (5x - 4)^{\circ}$ and $m\angle B = (3x + 10)^{\circ}$. Find the measure of $\angle A$.
questions.answer: Solution: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $(5x - 4) + (3x + 10) = 134 \Rightarrow 8x + 6 = 134 \Rightarrow 8x = 128 \Rightarrow x = 16.$ Substitute $x = 16$ into $m\angle A$: $m\angle A = 5(16) - 4 = 80 - 4 = 76^{\circ}.$
questions.explanation: Solution: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $(5x - 4) + (3x + 10) = 134 \Rightarrow 8x + 6 = 134 \Rightarrow 8x = 128 \Rightarrow x = 16.$ Substitute $x = 16$ into $m\angle A$: $m\angle A = 5(16) - 4 = 80 - 4 = 76^{\circ}.$

questions.q: In isosceles triangle $\Delta  PQR$, $PQ = PR$. The vertex angle $\angle P$ measures $40^{\circ}$. An angle bisector is drawn from base angle $\angle Q$ to point $D$ on side $PR$. What is the measure of $\angle QDR$?
questions.answer: Step 1: Find the base angles of $\Delta  PQR$: Since $PQ = PR$, the base angles $\angle Q$ and $\angle R$ are equal: $m\angle Q = m\angle R = \frac{180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}}{2} = \frac{140^{\circ}}{2} = 70^{\circ}.$ Step 2: Find the bisected angle measure: $QD$ bisects $\angle PQR$, so: $m\angle DQR = \frac{70^{\circ}}{2} = 35^{\circ}.$ Step 3: Apply the triangle angle sum to $\Delta  QDR$: $m\angle QDR = 180^{\circ} - (m\angle DQR + m\angle R) = 180^{\circ} - (35^{\circ} + 70^{\circ}) = 180^{\circ} - 105^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}.$
questions.explanation: Step 1: Find the base angles of $\Delta  PQR$: Since $PQ = PR$, the base angles $\angle Q$ and $\angle R$ are equal: $m\angle Q = m\angle R = \frac{180^{\circ} - 40^{\circ}}{2} = \frac{140^{\circ}}{2} = 70^{\circ}.$ Step 2: Find the bisected angle measure: $QD$ bisects $\angle PQR$, so: $m\angle DQR = \frac{70^{\circ}}{2} = 35^{\circ}.$ Step 3: Apply the triangle angle sum to $\Delta  QDR$: $m\angle QDR = 180^{\circ} - (m\angle DQR + m\angle R) = 180^{\circ} - (35^{\circ} + 70^{\circ}) = 180^{\circ} - 105^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}.$

questions.q: An equilateral triangle has side lengths of $12\ \mathrm{cm}$. An altitude is drawn from one vertex to the opposite side. Find the exact height and area of the triangle.
questions.answer: Solution: The altitude bisects the vertex angle into two $30^{\circ}$ angles and bisects the base into two equal segments of length $6\ \mathrm{cm}$, forming two congruent $30\mathrm{–}60\mathrm{–}90$ right triangles. The shorter leg opposite $30^{\circ}$ is $x = 6$. The altitude (height) is the longer leg opposite $60^{\circ}$: $h = x\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{cm}.$ Now compute the area using $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2} b h$: $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2} (12) (6\sqrt{3}) = 36\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{cm}^2.$
questions.explanation: Solution: The altitude bisects the vertex angle into two $30^{\circ}$ angles and bisects the base into two equal segments of length $6\ \mathrm{cm}$, forming two congruent $30\mathrm{–}60\mathrm{–}90$ right triangles. The shorter leg opposite $30^{\circ}$ is $x = 6$. The altitude (height) is the longer leg opposite $60^{\circ}$: $h = x\sqrt{3} = 6\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{cm}.$ Now compute the area using $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2} b h$: $\mathrm{Area} = \frac{1}{2} (12) (6\sqrt{3}) = 36\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{cm}^2.$

questions.q: Two similar cylinders have surface areas of $64\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2$ and $144\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^2$. If the volume of the smaller cylinder is $96\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^3$, find the volume of the larger cylinder.
questions.answer: Step 1: Find the area ratio and linear scale factor $k$: $\frac{\mathrm{Area}_2}{\mathrm{Area}_1} = \frac{144\pi}{64\pi} = \frac{9}{4} = k^2 \Rightarrow k = \sqrt{\frac{9}{4}} = \frac{3}{2}$ Step 2: Compute the volume ratio $k^3$: $\frac{\mathrm{Volume}_2}{\mathrm{Volume}_1} = k^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$ Step 3: Calculate the volume of the larger cylinder: $\mathrm{Volume}_2 = 96\pi \times \frac{27}{8} = 12\pi \times 27 = 324\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^3$
questions.explanation: Step 1: Find the area ratio and linear scale factor $k$: $\frac{\mathrm{Area}_2}{\mathrm{Area}_1} = \frac{144\pi}{64\pi} = \frac{9}{4} = k^2 \Rightarrow k = \sqrt{\frac{9}{4}} = \frac{3}{2}$ Step 2: Compute the volume ratio $k^3$: $\frac{\mathrm{Volume}_2}{\mathrm{Volume}_1} = k^3 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{27}{8}$ Step 3: Calculate the volume of the larger cylinder: $\mathrm{Volume}_2 = 96\pi \times \frac{27}{8} = 12\pi \times 27 = 324\pi\ \mathrm{cm}^3$

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Segment $AB$ has endpoints $A(2, -1)$ and $B(6, 7)$. Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ in slope-intercept form.
questions.answer: Solution: The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint and has a perpendicular slope. Step 1 (Midpoint): $M = \left(\frac{2 + 6}{2},\ \frac{-1 + 7}{2}\right) = (4, 3).$ Step 2 (Slope of AB): $m_{AB} = \frac{7 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2.$ Step 3 (Perpendicular slope): $m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{2}.$ Step 4 (Point-slope equation through M(4, 3)): $y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \Rightarrow y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2 \Rightarrow y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5.$
questions.explanation: Solution: The perpendicular bisector passes through the midpoint and has a perpendicular slope. Step 1 (Midpoint): $M = \left(\frac{2 + 6}{2},\ \frac{-1 + 7}{2}\right) = (4, 3).$ Step 2 (Slope of AB): $m_{AB} = \frac{7 - (-1)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2.$ Step 3 (Perpendicular slope): $m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{2}.$ Step 4 (Point-slope equation through M(4, 3)): $y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4) \Rightarrow y - 3 = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2 \Rightarrow y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5.$

questions.q: In $\Delta  PQR$, ray $QS$ bisects $\angle Q$ with $S$ lying on side $PR$. If $PQ = 14$, $QR = 21$, and $PR = 25$, find the length of segment $PS$.
questions.answer: Step 1: Apply the Angle Bisector Theorem: The bisector divides side $PR$ into segments proportional to the adjacent sides: $\frac{PS}{SR} = \frac{PQ}{QR} = \frac{14}{21} = \frac{2}{3}$ Step 2: Express $SR$ in terms of $PS$: Since $PS + SR = 25$, we have $SR = 25 - PS$: $\frac{PS}{25 - PS} = \frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow 3PS = 2(25 - PS) = 50 - 2PS$ Step 3: Solve for $PS$: $5PS = 50 \Rightarrow PS = 10 \quad (\mathrm{and\ } SR = 15).$
questions.explanation: Step 1: Apply the Angle Bisector Theorem: The bisector divides side $PR$ into segments proportional to the adjacent sides: $\frac{PS}{SR} = \frac{PQ}{QR} = \frac{14}{21} = \frac{2}{3}$ Step 2: Express $SR$ in terms of $PS$: Since $PS + SR = 25$, we have $SR = 25 - PS$: $\frac{PS}{25 - PS} = \frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow 3PS = 2(25 - PS) = 50 - 2PS$ Step 3: Solve for $PS$: $5PS = 50 \Rightarrow PS = 10 \quad (\mathrm{and\ } SR = 15).$

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the point $P$ on directed line segment from $A(-3, 2)$ to $B(7, 12)$ that partitions the segment in the ratio $2 : 3$.
questions.answer: Step 1: Determine the fractional distance: A ratio of $2 : 3$ means $P$ is $\frac{2}{2 + 3} = \frac{2}{5}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$. Step 2: Apply the partition formula: $x_P = x_1 + \frac{2}{5}(x_2 - x_1) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(7 - (-3)) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = -3 + 4 = 1.$ $y_P = y_1 + \frac{2}{5}(y_2 - y_1) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(12 - 2) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = 2 + 4 = 6.$ The partitioning point is $P(1, 6)$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Determine the fractional distance: A ratio of $2 : 3$ means $P$ is $\frac{2}{2 + 3} = \frac{2}{5}$ of the way from $A$ to $B$. Step 2: Apply the partition formula: $x_P = x_1 + \frac{2}{5}(x_2 - x_1) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(7 - (-3)) = -3 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = -3 + 4 = 1.$ $y_P = y_1 + \frac{2}{5}(y_2 - y_1) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(12 - 2) = 2 + \frac{2}{5}(10) = 2 + 4 = 6.$ The partitioning point is $P(1, 6)$.

questions.q: Triangle $\Delta  ABC$ has vertices $A(1, 2)$, $B(3, 2)$, and $C(1, 5)$. The triangle is dilated by a scale factor of $k = 3$ centered at the origin, and then translated by vector $\langle -2, 4 \rangle$. What are the coordinates of vertex $C''$?
questions.answer: Step 1: Dilation centered at the origin: Multiply each coordinate of $C(1, 5)$ by the scale factor $k = 3$: $C(1, 5) \longrightarrow C'(3 \times 1, 3 \times 5) = C'(3, 15).$ Step 2: Translation by vector $\langle -2, 4 \rangle$: Add $-2$ to the x-coordinate and $4$ to the y-coordinate: $C'(3, 15) \longrightarrow C''(3 - 2, 15 + 4) = C''(1, 19).$ The final coordinates of vertex $C''$ are $(1, 19)$.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Dilation centered at the origin: Multiply each coordinate of $C(1, 5)$ by the scale factor $k = 3$: $C(1, 5) \longrightarrow C'(3 \times 1, 3 \times 5) = C'(3, 15).$ Step 2: Translation by vector $\langle -2, 4 \rangle$: Add $-2$ to the x-coordinate and $4$ to the y-coordinate: $C'(3, 15) \longrightarrow C''(3 - 2, 15 + 4) = C''(1, 19).$ The final coordinates of vertex $C''$ are $(1, 19)$.

questions.q: A solid metal sphere of radius $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ is melted down and recast into a cylinder of radius $2\ \mathrm{cm}$. What is the height of the recast cylinder in cm?
questions.answer: Step 1: Calculate the volume of the sphere: $V_{\mathrm{sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi\mathrm{\ cm}^3.$ Step 2: Equate with the volume of the cylinder: $V_{\mathrm{cyl}} = \pi R^2 h = \pi (2^2) h = 4\pi h.$ Step 3: Solve for height $h$: $4\pi h = 36\pi \Rightarrow h = \frac{36\pi}{4\pi} = 9\mathrm{\ cm}.$ The height of the cylinder is $9$ cm.
questions.explanation: Step 1: Calculate the volume of the sphere: $V_{\mathrm{sphere}} = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3^3) = \frac{4}{3}\pi (27) = 36\pi\mathrm{\ cm}^3.$ Step 2: Equate with the volume of the cylinder: $V_{\mathrm{cyl}} = \pi R^2 h = \pi (2^2) h = 4\pi h.$ Step 3: Solve for height $h$: $4\pi h = 36\pi \Rightarrow h = \frac{36\pi}{4\pi} = 9\mathrm{\ cm}.$ The height of the cylinder is $9$ cm.

questions.q: Point $A(-2, 4)$ is reflected across the line $y = x$, and the resulting point is then translated by the vector $\langle 3, -1 \rangle$. What are the final coordinates?
questions.answer: Solution: Apply the transformations step by step: Step 1: Reflection across $y = x$ swaps the coordinates: $(x, y) \rightarrow (y, x)$: $A(-2, 4) \longrightarrow A'(4, -2).$ Step 2: Translation by $\langle 3, -1 \rangle$ adds 3 to the x-coordinate and subtracts 1 from the y-coordinate: $A'(4, -2) \longrightarrow A''(4 + 3, -2 - 1) = A''(7, -3).$ The final coordinates are $(7, -3)$.
questions.explanation: Solution: Apply the transformations step by step: Step 1: Reflection across $y = x$ swaps the coordinates: $(x, y) \rightarrow (y, x)$: $A(-2, 4) \longrightarrow A'(4, -2).$ Step 2: Translation by $\langle 3, -1 \rangle$ adds 3 to the x-coordinate and subtracts 1 from the y-coordinate: $A'(4, -2) \longrightarrow A''(4 + 3, -2 - 1) = A''(7, -3).$ The final coordinates are $(7, -3)$.

questions.q: An angle measures $10^\circ$. Find the measure of its complement.
questions.answer: Applying Angles principles, $90-10=80^\circ$. Therefore, the verified correct option is 80.

questions.q: In the diagram below, lines $m$ and $n$ are parallel. A transversal line intersects $m$ and $n$. Another line segment connects a point on $m$ to a point on $n$, forming a "crook-angle". Given that $\angle 1 = 120^\circ$ and $\angle 2 = 135^\circ$, what is the measure of the "crook-angle" $\angle 3$?
questions.answer: To solve this problem, we construct an auxiliary line through the vertex of $\angle 3$ that is parallel to lines $m$ and $n$. Let's call this auxiliary line $p$. This construction divides $\angle 3$ into two angles, let's call them $\angle 3a$ and $\angle 3b$, such that $\angle 3 = \angle 3a + \angle 3b$. Since line $m$ is parallel to line $p$, and the transversal that forms $\angle 1$ intersects both $m$ and $p$, $\angle 1$ and $\angle 3a$ are consecutive interior angles if we extend the transversal line. However, a more direct approach is to consider the relationship with $\angle 1$. The angle supplementary to $\angle 1$ is $180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$. This $60^\circ$ angle and $\angle 3a$ are alternate interior angles with respect to the transversal and parallel lines $m$ and $p$. Therefore, $\angle 3a = 60^\circ$. Now consider line $n$ parallel to line $p$. The transversal that forms $\angle 2$ intersects both $n$ and $p$. The angle supplementary to $\angle 2$ is $180^\circ - 135^\circ = 45^\circ$. This $45^\circ$ angle and $\angle 3b$ are alternate interior angles with respect to the transversal and parallel lines $n$ and $p$. Therefore, $\angle 3b = 45^\circ$. The total "crook-angle" $\angle 3$ is the sum of $\angle 3a$ and $\angle 3b$. So, $\angle 3 = \angle 3a + \angle 3b = 60^\circ + 45^\circ = 105^\circ$.

questions.q: Two parallel lines, $p$ and $q$, are intersected by a transversal line $t$. A pair of consecutive interior angles have measures $(4x + 9)^\circ$ and $(2x + 33)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: By the Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem, when two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, consecutive interior angles are supplementary (their measures sum to $180^\circ$). Set up the equation: $(4x + 9) + (2x + 33) = 180$ Combine like terms: $6x + 42 = 180$ Subtract $42$ from both sides: $6x = 138$ Divide by $6$: $x = 23$ Evaluating the angle measures at $x = 23$ gives $4(23) + 9 = 101^\circ$ and $2(23) + 33 = 79^\circ$, which are supplementary ($101^\circ + 79^\circ = 180^\circ$). Common Misconceptions: - Choice A ($8$): Mistakenly assumes consecutive interior angles are complementary, solving $6x + 42 = 90$. - Choice B ($12$): Confuses consecutive interior angles with alternate interior angles and sets them equal, solving $4x + 9 = 2x + 33$. - Choice D ($37$): Makes an algebraic sign error by adding $42$ to $180$ instead of subtracting, solving $6x = 222$.

Common Misconceptions: - Choice A ($8$): Mistakenly assumes consecutive interior angles are complementary, solving $6x + 42 = 90$. - Choice B ($12$): Confuses consecutive interior angles with alternate interior angles and sets them equal, solving $4x + 9 = 2x + 33$. - Choice D ($37$): Makes an algebraic sign error by adding $42$ to $180$ instead of subtracting, solving $6x = 222$.

questions.q: Two angles form a linear pair. The measures of the angles are $(3x + 10)^\circ$ and $(2x + 20)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: By definition, two angles that form a linear pair are adjacent and supplementary, meaning the sum of their measures is equal to $180^\circ$. Set up the algebraic equation: $(3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180$ Combine like terms: $5x + 30 = 180$ Subtract 30 from both sides: $5x = 150$ Divide both sides by 5: $x = 30$ Analysis of incorrect choices: - Choice A (10): Results from setting the two expressions equal to each other ($3x + 10 = 2x + 20$), confusing a linear pair with vertical angles. - Choice B (12): Results from setting the sum equal to $90^\circ$ instead of $180^\circ$ ($5x + 30 = 90$), confusing supplementary angles with complementary angles. - Choice D (100): Results from solving for the measure of the larger angle, $3(30) + 10 = 100^\circ$, rather than the value of $x$.

Set up the algebraic equation: $(3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180$ Combine like terms: $5x + 30 = 180$ Subtract 30 from both sides: $5x = 150$ Divide both sides by 5: $x = 30$ Analysis of incorrect choices: - Choice A (10): Results from setting the two expressions equal to each other ($3x + 10 = 2x + 20$), confusing a linear pair with vertical angles. - Choice B (12): Results from setting the sum equal to $90^\circ$ instead of $180^\circ$ ($5x + 30 = 90$), confusing supplementary angles with complementary angles. - Choice D (100): Results from solving for the measure of the larger angle, $3(30) + 10 = 100^\circ$, rather than the value of $x$.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures $144^\circ$. If a second angle forms a pair of vertical angles with it, what is the measure of the second angle?

questions.q: An angle measures 3 times its supplement. What is the measure of the angle?
questions.answer: Let the supplement be $s$. Then angle $=3s$ and $s+3s=180$, so $s=45^\circ$ and the angle $=3\times45=135^\circ$.

questions.q: An angle measures 5 times its complement. What is the measure of the angle?

questions.answer: Corresponding angles are equal: $6x+1=5x+6$. Solving gives $x=5$, so each angle $=6(5)+1=31^\circ$.
